text.p: Tim Wakefield allowed one hit in seven scoreless innings and Mo Vaughn homered for the first time this season as the Boston Red Sox routed the Oakland Athletics 10-1 with a 14-hit attack Monday.
Wakefield (1-1) allowed a double to Damon Mashore to open the game, then retired 20 straight hitters before walking Mark McGwire with two out in the seventh.
Vaughn's homer, which gave him his first RBI of the year, was a solo shot with two outs in the bottom of the first.
"The important thing is that when you're not feeling well is to try and get your hits," said Vaughn. "I want to drive the ball though. It's good to get the first one."

Wakefield was coming off his shortest outing as a member of the Red Sox -- 2 2/3 innings in Oakland on April 8. He struck out two and walked one. He threw just 76 pitches before being relieved by Rick Trlicek.
"When it's cold like this it's kind of hard to feel the ball sometimes. I was able to overcome that early," Wakefield said. "It felt OK."
Willie Adams (0-1) took the loss, allowing seven runs and nine hits in five innings.

Bill Haselman went 2-for-4, including his first home run of the season. The bottom of Boston's lineup -- Haselman, Wil Cordero and Darren Bragg -- combined to go 7-of-12 with five RBI and five runs scored.
Jose Canseco was 0-for-4 in his return to Fenway Park. Canseco, who played two seasons for the Red Sox, was traded back to the A's for pitcher John Wasdin in an off-season deal.
"Wakefield did a great job. His knuckleball was dancing everywhere," Canseco said. "When he's on like that, he's going to be tough to hit."

In Baltimore, former Twin Scott Erickson allowed five hits over eight innings to win his first two decisions for the first time in his career, as the Orioles won their fourth straight, 4-2 over Minnesota.
Erickson, who had a lifetime record of 5-15 in April, had his sinker working as he recorded 16 groundouts. He also picked up his first win in three starts against his former team.

B.J. Surhoff's bases-loaded single capped a three-run third inning that gave the Orioles a 3-2 lead. Brady Anderson and Cal Ripken each had two hits for Baltimore, which has the American League's best record at 8-2. The Orioles also are off to the third-best 10-game start in team history.
Bob Tewksbury (0-2) took the loss.
In Cleveland, Dennis Martinez allowed two hits over six innings against his former team and three relievers held the Indians hitless over the final three frames as the Seattle Mariners won 6-1.

Martinez (1-0) allowed one earned run while walking four and striking out one to pick up the victory after the Indians had pounded him for seven runs and 11 hits in four innings in his first start of the season.
Russ Davis went 3-for-4 with a solo homer for the Mariners, who won for the fifth time in six games. Jay Buhner had two hits, scored twice and drove in a pair of runs.
Charles Nagy (1-1) allowed five earned runs and nine hits in seven innings.

In New York, Jason Dickson allowed five hits over seven innings and struck out a career-high seven as the California Angels handed the Yankees their first consecutive home losses since last July, 5-1.

Dickson (2-0) allowed one run, walked three and lowered his ERA to 3.10. He benefited from a four-run seventh inning, capped by a two-run homer by former Yankee Jim Leyritz. Mike Holtz finished up with two hitless innings.

Yankees starter Kenny Rogers (0-1) allowed no hits until Jim Edmonds had an infield single with one out in the fifth. But Rogers allowed a game-tying solo homer to Darin Erstad in the sixth and got into trouble in the seventh.
Leyritz, returning to Yankee Stadium after an off-season trade, received a standing ovation before his first at-bat.
In Texas, Rusty Greer blasted a tie-breaking two-run homer run in the eighth to lift the Rangers past the Chicago White Sox, 3-1.
Danny Patterson (1-1) pitched a scoreless eighth inning to earn his first major-league win. John Wetteland pitched the ninth for the save. Wilson Alvarez (0-3) took the loss.
In Milwaukee, Cal Eldred hurled eight shutout innings and Jeromy Burnitz's run-scoring single snapped a scoreless tie and triggered a three-run sixth as the Brewers blanked the Detroit Tigers 7-0.
Eldred (2-0), who scattered four hits with three walks and two strikeouts, increased his streak of scoreless innings against Detroit to 14. Doug Jones struck out two in the ninth.

In Toronto, Johnny Damon scored from first on Bip Roberts' hit-and-run single to centre off Paul Quantrill (0-1) with two out in the eighth inning, lifting the Kansas City Royals to a 3-2 victory over the Blue Jays.
Glendon Rusch (2-0) allowed two runs and seven hits over seven innings as he won for the second time in as many major-league starts. The 22-year-old left-hander lowered his ERA to 1.20.
